findings.claim: The decimal formatter now uses the fixed-point 'F' format without a precision specifier, whose default is two fractional digits. Values such as 123.456m therefore serialize as "123.46" instead of "123.456", changing the established wire bytes and losing data on deserialization; this unrelated change is not required by the code-coverage feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Using otherwise identical serializers built from base and head, serialize decimal values 123.456m, 0.005m, and 1.2300m with DecimalFormatter (via MessagePackSerializer.Serialize<decimal> under the standard resolver). Compare the MessagePack string bytes and deserialize each head payload to confirm that 123.456m becomes 123.46m.
